paths.description: Homepage and primary lottery-results surface; representative of the dense results template and first-load consent journey.
Northern lottery detail page; representative of regional result tables and filter forms.
Statistics section/listing; representative of data-analysis navigation and cards.
Privacy policy content page; representative of long-form editorial/legal content and no-JS delivery.
Unknown URL requested to inspect HTTP failure handling; server returned HTTP 404.

findings.summary: No user-preference dark theme
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually unchanged from the light capture, and the computed probe reports colorScheme "normal" with no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface/text colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route and state changes lack transition continuity
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition rules on a multi-page site with many regional navigation routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin route changes, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long pages provide weak position and attention cues
findings.evidence: Representative pages are 4,376 to 14,174 CSS pixels tall, while the probe found no scroll-state, scroll marker, or transition mechanisms to orient users.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a compact sticky/scroll-state-aware header and clear current-location/progress cues without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Consent interstitial obscures the core content on every primary path
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile first-load screenshots show a modal consent wall covering the results, statistics, and navigation before the user can inspect the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface that keeps the core content visible, preserves equally prominent accept/reject choices, and supports light dismiss where legally appropriate.

findings.summary: Dense chrome and advertising crowd the content
findings.evidence: Mobile captures show a crowded horizontal navigation, large ad slot, repeated colored borders, and long dense result tables; the content extends beyond 12,000 CSS pixels on key pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Simplify repeated chrome, reserve smaller ad regions, and establish a calmer content hierarchy with readable spacing and grouping.

findings.summary: Components rely on page-level sizing rather than container responsiveness
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found no @container rules across reused cards/tables, although the site reuses those components across sidebars and full-width mobile layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type and component-level queries for reusable navigation, result, and statistics components.

findings.summary: Many controls are undersized and keyboard focus is invisible
findings.evidence: The active probe found 200 visible interactive elements below 44px in at least one dimension; focusing the first visible control yielded outline style "none".
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible :focus-visible styling and enlarge or pad controls to robust touch-target sizes without relying on hover.

findings.summary: Dynamic result state is not exposed as a clear recoverable status
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM uses repeated waiting.gif placeholders for live result state, but no semantic dialog/details primitives or observable live-status treatment was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose loading, updated, empty, and error states with readable status text, aria-live where appropriate, and retry/recovery controls.

findings.summary: Largest content appears too late and delivery delays rendering
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 8.9s, TTI 13.3s and performance 0.65; the trace measured LCP 4.99s and the HAR found 60 requests/1.44MB with render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP resource, shorten render-blocking chains, defer non-critical advertising, and verify LCP below 2.5s under mobile conditions.

findings.summary: Third-party and unused code dominate the load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 638KiB unused JavaScript and 25KiB unused CSS; HAR attributes 1.407MB and 52 of 60 requests to third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove low-value vendors, conditionally load advertising/analytics after consent and intent, and split or eliminate unused first-party code.

findings.summary: Lottery data tables lack semantic headers and captions
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 8 large tables whose td cells lack headers and 4 tables using colspan cells instead of caption elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use caption, thead, th, scope, and headers/id relationships so row and column context is announced by assistive technology.

findings.summary: Core navigation and result text fail contrast minimums
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 88 contrast failures, including white on #ff6600 at 2.93:1 and navigation text on #ed1c25 at 4.38:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG contrast for normal and large text, then re-test all recurring templates.

findings.summary: Focus and document structure are not robust
findings.evidence: The focus probe returned no visible outline, the homepage contains four h1 elements, and authored templates use div role=main rather than a main element.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single main landmark, rationalize heading levels, and ensure every interactive component has an obvious :focus-visible state in reading order.

findings.summary: Asset and platform hygiene needs cleanup
findings.evidence: Images evidence found one image without dimensions; Lighthouse reports a deprecated Topics API call from advertising code and inspector cookie issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions and remove or update third-party code that invokes deprecated APIs or creates browser inspector issues.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security headers and cookie protections are missing
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; all three observed cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; set appropriate Secure/SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: The first load has an excessive tracking and advertising footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 27 third-party origins and 11 known tracker domains; HAR recorded 52 third-party requests and 1.407MB before consent interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics and ad auctions until consent, reduce the vendor list substantially, and batch/minimize retained analytics data.

findings.summary: Layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient
findings.evidence: Although html lang="vi" is correct, the CSS probe found no logical-property usage and 45 physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use inline/block logical properties and verify translated or bidirectional content does not break layout.

findings.summary: Date rendering appears hand-formatted and locale-bound
findings.evidence: Rendered pages contain recurring DD-MM-YYYY strings, while the authored DOM probe found no Intl usage in date-heavy result templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Store dates unambiguously and format them through Intl.DateTimeFormat for the selected locale.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses straightforward efficiency improvements
findings.evidence: Images evidence found 9 legacy-format images, 8 below-fold images without lazy loading, and 3 images without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert suitable assets to AVIF/WebP, lazy-load below-fold content, retain dimensions, and provide responsive sources where display sizes vary.

findings.summary: The runtime footprint is disproportionate for a results page
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 607,683 nodes/33.4MB and the post-scroll capture 696,103 nodes/37.8MB; the DOM probe counted 6,857 elements. Cross-session variance makes leak attribution low-confidence, but the absolute footprint is high.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce third-party runtimes and DOM duplication, virtualize or paginate long repeated content, then repeat same-session baseline/final heap analysis.

taskList.title: Delay and reduce advertising/tracking until valid consent
Fix LCP and critical resource delivery
Restore table semantics, contrast, landmarks, focus, and target sizes
Deploy defensive headers and secure cookie attributes
Simplify mobile chrome and add clear live/recovery states
Add preference-driven dark theme and component responsiveness
Optimize images and investigate DOM/heap growth
Modernize locale, transitions, and browser hygiene
